newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks close at another record high.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks close at another record high.

text.p: Australian stocks closed at another record high on Monday with banks and insurers leading the charge as investors went chasing high yield stocks ahead of another expected local interest rate cut.
The All Ordinaries index set its third successive record closing high, ending 14 points firmer at 2669.3 and just short of its all-time record of 2670.0 also set during Monday trade.
Trade was brisk with about A$840 million (US$630 million) worth of stocks traded. Traders said the continued rises showed the market was expecting another cut in official interest rates.
"That is why all the interest rate-sensitive stocks moved," said Robert Osbourn, analyst at fund manager Tyndall Australia.
Osbourn said it appeared the Australian government was hoping for more rate cuts.
Treasurer Peter Costello said in Parliament that the government projected an outlook of falling interest rates.
"A lot of the top 20 stocks are running. I think if the market starts to get overvalued, that is where you have to be because that is where the solid security is," Osbourn said.

Both the bank and insurers' indices were up more than one percent with the Commonwealth Bank recording the biggest jump of over three percent. ANZ shares also performed strongly and recovered all of Friday's losses to close up 20 cents at A$9.85.
Insurer QBE hit a record high of A$8.30 in line with other interest rate-sensitive stocks.
BHP remained indifferent to the general market rise and closed one cent up at A$18.90 as concerns lingered over operational issues and output at its Ok Tedi copper mine.
